ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the points A, B, C, D, and E are on the same straight line, with point D being the midpoint of segment AB, and point E being the midpoint of segment BC. If the length of segment AC is 12, what is the length of segment DE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $D$ is the midpoint of the line segment $AB$, it follows that $AD=BD$,\\
Since $E$ is the midpoint of the line segment $BC$, it follows that $BE=CE$,\\
Given that $AC=12$, it follows that $AD+CD=12$, hence $BD+CD=12$,\\
Additionally, since $BD=2CE+CD$, it follows that $2CE+CD+CD=12$,\\
which simplifies to $2(CE+CD)=12$, hence $CE+CD=6$,\\
meaning the length of the segment $DE$ equals $\boxed{6}$.
